notes: INSTRUMENT BALANCES NOW MEAN ONE THING: VALUE TODAY. Engine work only; the page merge, rename and Instruments removal are deliberately NOT in this build. ROOT CAUSE, found in the code rather than inferred: inv.balance was documented two contradictory ways in the same file — 'current opening balances which already reflect logged tx' at the actuals overlay, and 'the horizon-start seed used to project the PAST' at applyTransactionDelta. Worse, the two sides were asymmetric: a logged REDEMPTION reduced inv.balance, a logged CONTRIBUTION did not. So the field behaved as today's value when selling and as a stale historical seed when buying, and no consistent reading of the data was possible. The engine then seeded that figure at the horizon start and re-added every logged contribution on top, double-counting them. Because each page runs the projection from a different month, each double-counted a different subset — which is why Bonds read Rs 2,00,000 on the sheet and Rs 2,40,284 on Net Worth. THE FIX, three parts. Contributions now move the instrument balance exactly as redemptions always did, so both sides are symmetric. The engine anchors its series to TODAY rather than to the horizon start: months from today forward project from the stored figure, and months before it are walked BACK through logged events, the same pattern savings already uses. And the overlay no longer re-adds logged contributions, since they are already inside the balance. GROWTH IS NOT AUTO-APPLIED between edits, by choice. Compounding the stored figure silently would mean it is no longer the number the user typed. Contributions and redemptions are events the app observes; market movement is not. A balanceAsOf stamp is now recorded on every logged contribution and redemption so staleness can be surfaced in the UI later. PAST MONTHS ARE WALKED BACK WITHOUT UN-APPLYING GROWTH. Logged events are real; inferred history is not, and reconstructing a precise past value the user never recorded would be invention. STRESS TESTED, FIVE SCENARIOS, ALL PASSING. Logging a Rs 50,000 contribution moves the stored balance by exactly Rs 50,000 and the projection by Rs 40,000, the difference being the Rs 10,000 scheduled contribution it absorbs. A Rs 70,000 redemption moves both by exactly minus Rs 70,000. Three instruments report identical figures whether the projection starts in May, October or the current month — previously Bonds differed by Rs 40,284, FD by Rs 4,50,000 and Mutual Funds by Rs 1,79,716, and monthly-compounding instruments drifted further the longer the window. Stored plus this month's scheduled contribution equals the projected figure for every instrument. Closing still zeroes the balance from the close month. PERMANENT GUARD ADDED to the regression: an instrument must report the same figure whether the projection runs from the horizon start or from the sheet's window start, and the check fails loudly otherwise. Six separate implementations of shared quantities have surfaced in this codebase and an assertion is the only thing that has reliably stopped them returning. Currently reporting a zero mismatch. ACTION REQUIRED BEFORE TRUSTING THE NUMBERS: re-enter the current balance for EVERY instrument once. Contributions logged before this build were never added to the stored figures, and the engine will no longer add them on the user's behalf. Bonds, FD and Mutual Funds were already typed as current values and should be close; Physical gold and Stocks still hold their original May figures and will understate by the October gold purchases and the Jio IPO until re-entered. This could not be migrated automatically — distinguishing an edited balance from an untouched one is not possible from the data, and guessing would risk re-creating the exact double-count being fixed.
